title: Openness of the fibre Cohen-Macaulay locus between affine schemes
statement: Let $X,T$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme; def-weil-affine-spectrum], meaning schemes isomorphic to spectra of commutative rings. Let $f:X\to T$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The set of points $y\in X$ where the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth] of the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(y)}$ at $y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre; def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] equals its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is open in $X$.

source.place: Tags 00RI and 00RH (affine openness), 00N8 (Cohen-Macaulay self-module); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00RI and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00RH, read 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Fix y in the fibre depth-equals-dimension locus. The quasi-finite polynomial chart theorem supplies an affine open U containing y, a natural number n equal to the topological fibre dimension at y, and a locally finitely presented quasi-finite map e to affine n-space over T, factoring f on U.

The chart target and source are affine. Openness of flatness for the self-module of their coordinate rings gives an open stalk-flat locus F in U. The Lean proof identifies Spec-map stalks with prime localizations, uses flatness over a localized base iff flatness over the base, transfers between LocalizedModule and Localization.AtPrime using IsLocalizedModule.iso, and pulls the result back through the canonical affine scheme isomorphisms. This proves isOpen_flat_stalks_affine without a Noetherian base.

The pointwise criterion and the depth and dimension hypotheses put the point of U over y in F. Every point of F has a fibre stalk of depth equal to dimension by that criterion. The image of F under the open immersion U into X is open, contains y and is contained in the desired locus. Apply isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open to finish; the empty-source case is vacuous.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00RH: choose the polynomial chart, apply the pointwise fibre criterion and openness of flatness, and assemble open neighborhoods. K3 Lean reduction uses two new statements and proves the affine flat-locus transport and neighborhood assembly.

lean.statement:
theorem isOpen_fibre_depth_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isAffine
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine T]
    (f : X ⟶ T) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] :
    IsOpen {y : X |
      (IsLocalRing.depth (R := (f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y))
        ((f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y)) : WithBot ℕ∞) =
          ringKrullDim ((f.fiber (f y)).presheaf.stalk (f.asFiber y))}
